newsitem.title: UK: Morgan Stanley pays Mirror pensioners - Times.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley pays Mirror pensioners - Times.

text.p: A subsidiary of U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley has paid about 15 million pounds to settle the final legal action brought by the Mirror Group Plc pension scheme following the death of media tycoon Robert Maxwell, The Times newspaper reported on Saturday.
The pension fund took legal action after hundreds of millions of pounds were found to be missing from the pension funds of companies run by then Mirror chairman Maxwell, who died in November 1991.
Morgan Stanley Trust Co was one of the custodians of shares owned by the Miror scheme that were used as collateral for loans to Maxwell private companies in the months before he died.
After calling in the loans, the banks refused to return the assets to the pensions funds, triggering a flurry of lawsuits.
Neither Morgan Stanley nor Mirror pension trustees could be reached for comment, but the Times said both had confirmed that a confidential settlement had been reached.

The paper said the deal, along with payments made by other financial firms as part of a 276 million pound global settlement, meant the pensions of present and past employees of the Maxwell publishing empire were secured.
It said that as a result of the settlement the Mirror scheme was in surplus for the first time since the shortfall was discovered.
